import torch
import torch.nn as nn


class TensorFunctorAttention(nn.Module):
    """Coordinate-free sequence mixing layer.

    The projection is applied along the channel axis wherever it lives in the
    tensor layout.  All remaining axes are treated as an arbitrary batch of
    coordinates, so the module works for any spatial/sequence size, any number
    of leading (e.g. vmapped) batch dimensions, and inside `torch.vmap` /
    autograd graphs.  No indexing, no in-place writes, no Python loops.
    """

    def __init__(self, dim: int = 16):
        super().__init__()
        self.dim = int(dim)
        self.proj = nn.Linear(self.dim, self.dim)

    def _channel_axis(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> int:
        """Locate the channel axis in a layout-independent way."""
        shape = tuple(x.shape)
        ndim = len(shape)

        if ndim == 0:
            raise ValueError(f"TensorFunctorAttention expects at least 1D input, got shape {shape}")

        # Canonical (N, C, *spatial) layout.
        if ndim >= 2 and shape[1] == self.dim:
            return 1
        # Layouts where the batch axis has been stripped (e.g. vmap over batch).
        if shape[0] == self.dim:
            return 0
        # Channels-last layout.
        if ndim >= 2 and shape[-1] == self.dim:
            return ndim - 1

        # No axis matches the projection width: fall back to the canonical
        # channel axis and let nn.Linear raise a descriptive error.
        if ndim >= 2:
            return 1
        return 0

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        axis = self._channel_axis(x)

        # Move the channel axis to the end, apply the linear map there, and
        # move it back.  Everything else is carried along as batch.
        if axis != x.dim() - 1:
            x = x.movedim(axis, -1)
            out = self.proj(x)
            return out.movedim(-1, axis)

        return self.proj(x)

    # Make the module friendly to functional/vmap-style calls.
    def __repr__(self) -> str:  # pragma: no cover - cosmetic
        return f"TensorFunctorAttention(dim={self.dim})"

import torch
import torch.nn as nn


class TensorFunctorAttention(nn.Module):
    """Coordinate-free sequence mixer.

    The projection is applied uniformly along the channel dimension while every
    other (batch / spatial / sequence) dimension is left untouched, so the
    module behaves as a functor: any input shape is mapped to an output of the
    same shape. Because no Python-level indexing, in-place assignment or
    fixed-size slicing is used, the module is fully compatible with
    ``torch.vmap`` and with autograd.
    """

    def __init__(self, dim: int = 16):
        super().__init__()
        self.dim = dim
        self.proj = nn.Linear(dim, dim)

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        if x.dim() < 2:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Expected input with at least 2 dimensions (..., channel, ...), "
                f"got shape {tuple(x.shape)}"
            )

        channels = x.shape[1]
        if channels != self.dim:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Expected {self.dim} channels, got {channels} for input shape "
                f"{tuple(x.shape)}"
            )

        # Move the channel axis to the end so that `nn.Linear` (which operates
        # on the last dimension) can be applied to every spatial position at
        # once. This works for (B, C), (B, C, H), (B, C, H, W), ... and for
        # batched/vmapped variants of those shapes.
        x_channels_last = x.movedim(1, -1)
        out_channels_last = self.proj(x_channels_last)
        out = out_channels_last.movedim(-1, 1)

        return out

    assumes a particular number of spatial dimensions or batch size, so it is

    ``torch.func.grad``/``autograd``, and with inputs whose spatial/sequence
    dimensions change between calls.

import torch
import torch.nn as nn


class MorphismEncoder(nn.Module):
    """Coordinate-free sequence/channel mixing layer.

    The projection acts purely on the feature (``dim``) axis and is completely
    agnostic of every other axis: batch and arbitrary trailing spatial/sequence
    dimensions are carried through as opaque batch dimensions.  Because the
    forward pass contains no Python loops, no index-based slicing and no hard
    coded shape assumptions, it composes cleanly with ``torch.vmap`` (functorch)
    and with autograd, and it keeps working when the spatial/sequence rank or
    size changes between training and evaluation.

    def __init__(self, dim: int = 16):
        super().__init__()
        self.dim = dim
        self.proj = nn.Linear(dim, dim)

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:

        if x.dim() <= 1 or x.shape[-1] == self.dim:
            return self.proj(x)

        # Channel-first layout: (batch, dim, *spatial) -> (batch, *spatial, dim)
        x_last = x.movedim(1, -1)
        out = self.proj(x_last)
        return out.movedim(-1, 1)
